facts.statement: MME-1367 requires Aleph, Funes, Menard, Kilgore, and Burdgeon to consume one sanitized executable fixture.
Menard and Kilgore have no domain contracts yet, while Aleph and Funes have active uncommitted contract work.

assumptions.statement: Synthetic content modeled on observed Landing contract structure preserves the required semantics without exposing private conversation content.

decisions.decision: Use a test-only Composer package as the shared fixture authority.
decisions.rationale: It prevents application ownership and repository-local fixture drift.

constraints: The package contains no domain behavior.
Provider-specific identifiers stop after the Aleph expected boundary.
No application database identity, personal path, credential, or live conversation content enters the fixture.

open_questions.question: Which public Menard and Kilgore value types will adopt their expected fixture sections?
Should the package be published remotely or consumed as a path development dependency until the contract stabilizes?

glossary.definition: The expected output owned by one package and chained to references from the preceding section.
A named fact omitted from accepted history so completeness behavior can be verified.

content_opportunities.user_problem: Cross-repository acceptance tests drift when each package owns a copy of the scenario.
content_opportunities.concept: Chain stable identities through one data-only fixture while keeping domain assertions in their owning packages.
content_opportunities.hook: A shared fixture can connect packages without becoming a shared domain model.
